Reading a Part Number Built to a Customer's Print

Not every SBS item follows the standard fastener convention. /250600002PR-EV is a non-standard number: it carries a customer part number, a note that the part is made per print, and a tag for its Electric Vehicle application. This module walks through it end to end.

Topic T3 · Plastite 48-2 Thread Form

What Is Plastite 48-2?

“PLASTIT” in the item description points to a Plastite thread-forming screw: a fastener that cuts or forms its own mating thread as it is driven into plastic.

Plastite 48-2 thread form: side view (left) and cross-sections (right). Click to enlarge.

Twin Lead, 48°

Two thread starts run side by side at a 48° thread angle, so the screw advances quickly and grips the plastic it forms.

1–2 Thread Tapered Lead

The first one to two threads taper down to a point, which helps the screw start straight in the hole.

Thread-Forming Nodes

The rounded lobes of the cross-section do the forming work. They push the thread into the plastic as the screw turns.

Relief Areas

The flatter areas between the lobes give displaced material room to move, which keeps driving torque in check.

Topic T4 · Case Hardening

Case Hardening

A thread-forming screw has two jobs that pull in opposite directions: its threads must be hard enough to form a thread, and its body tough enough not to snap. Case hardening gives it both.

The outer surface is case hardened; the inner surface remains soft and tough.

Outer Surface: Case Hardened

Only the skin of the part is hardened, giving a hard, wear-resistant surface where the threads do their work.

Inner Core: Soft and Tough

The inside stays soft and tough, so the screw can absorb load and flex without breaking.

The hard case that makes the screw work is also what makes it sensitive to hydrogen. Continue to .

Topic T5 · Hydrogen Embrittlement

Hydrogen Embrittlement

Hardened, high-strength steel can be damaged by hydrogen. The screw can look fine and still crack under load, sometimes long after it was installed.

How it happens: diffusion, accumulation, then crack initiation and propagation.
1

Diffusion

Hydrogen atoms enter the steel and move through its grain structure.

2

Accumulation

The hydrogen collects at grain boundaries and stress points, weakening the metal there.

3

Crack Initiation & Propagation

A crack starts and grows until the part fails.

What it can look like: a failed hardened bolt, with the red circles marking the damaged areas.

Why It Matters for This Part

Hardened steel is the most susceptible, and processes such as plating can introduce hydrogen. That is why a post-plating bake is a common safeguard for case-hardened fasteners like this one.

Reference

Glossary

Every code, acronym, and standard used in this module, defined in plain language. Tap a term's "jump" button to see it in context.

Case Hardening

A heat-treating process that hardens only the outer surface of a steel part, leaving the inner core soft and tough.

Customer Part Number

The number a customer uses for the part in their own system. In /250600002PR-EV, 250600002 is the customer part number.

EV (Electric Vehicle)

The final element of the part number. It tags the part for an electric vehicle application.

Hydrogen Embrittlement

A failure mode in which hydrogen diffuses into hardened steel, accumulates at grain boundaries, and leads to crack initiation and propagation.

Non-Standard Part

An item that does not follow the standard SBS fastener numbering. A leading slash, as in /250600002PR-EV, marks it as non-standard.

Per Print (PR)

Made to the customer's engineering print rather than to a catalog standard.

Plastite 48-2

A thread-forming screw design for plastics, with a twin lead, 48° thread, a tapered lead, and thread-forming nodes separated by relief areas.
